title: Not quite the "poor man's mini split" I was hoping for- heat requires water removal!
text:
Not quite the "poor man's mini split" I was hoping for- heat requires water removal!. Portable AC units are great for times a traditional window unit isn't an option. However, I was particularly interested in this one because of the supplemental HEAT function as well.
You see, I have a room that was added on to my home without attaching to the house's central HVAC. It is always noticeably hotter in the summer and colder in the winter in that room. I looked into installing an efficient mini-split unit which would solve this problem, however I could not justify the cost (thousands of dollars!).
This unit seemed like a possible work around: I can either pipe it to a window or drill a hole in my wall to pipe it out of (still much cheaper than a mini split!!), and have supplemental cooling AND heating!
Well, it turns out, using any mode other than cooling requires you to empty a water bucket. Dehumidify I understand, but I was surprised to learn that the heat pump mode (essentially running the AC in reverse) also fills with water and requires draining. There was not a lot of information about the heat mode before ordering it, and now I see why. It really does seem to be an afterthought, the cooling mode is the important feature. I'm disappointed because that mode was the only thing that stood out between this and other portable AC units I was looking at. It seems like still a good air conditioner if you've got a space that needs a portable one, but I wouldn't get it for the supplemental heating mode.
